title: It takes courage to be creative, with Zorana Ivcevic Pringle, PhD

sentences.en: Most of us don't lack creative ideas.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人并不缺乏创意。

sentences.en: Think about the last time you solved a problem in an unexpected way.
sentences.zh: 回想一下，你上一次用意想不到的方式解决问题是什么时候。

sentences.en: Maybe you figured out a shortcut at work or improvised a meal from the leftovers in your fridge.
sentences.zh: 也许你在工作中想出了一个捷径，或者用冰箱里的剩菜即兴做了一顿饭。

sentences.en: We don't always label those everyday moments as creative, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，我们并不总是把那些日常生活中的时刻贴上创意的标签。

sentences.en: Instead, we think of creativity as making art or music, and we assume that it's something you're born with, not something you can cultivate.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们认为创意就是创作艺术或音乐，并且我们认为这是天生具备的，而不是可以培养的。

sentences.en: But psychologist research suggests that creativity isn't just about flashes of brilliance or artistic talent.
sentences.zh: 但心理学研究表明，创意不仅仅是灵光一现或艺术才华。

sentences.en: It's about how we approach problems, respond to challenges, and turn our ideas into reality.
sentences.zh: 它关乎我们如何看待问题、应对挑战，以及将想法变为现实。

sentences.en: So what does it mean to be creative?
sentences.zh: 那么，有创意意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: What gets in the way of creative thinking, and how can we move past those barriers?
sentences.zh: 是什么阻碍了创造性思维，我们又该如何跨越这些障碍？

sentences.en: How do emotions and our social environments shape our creativity?
sentences.zh: 情绪和我们的社会环境如何塑造我们的创造力？

sentences.en: What is human creativity worth in a world being reshaped by AI?
sentences.zh: 在被人工智能重塑的世界里，人类的创造力价值何在？

sentences.en: And how can you move your creative ideas out of your head and into the world?
sentences.zh: 你又该如何将你的创意从脑海中付诸世界？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学话你知》（Speaking of Psychology），这是美国心理学协会的旗舰播客，探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Zorana Icevich Pringle.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是佐拉娜·伊切维奇·普林格尔博士。
zh_words: 佐拉娜·伊切维奇·普林格尔

sentences.en: Dr. Pringle is a senior research scientist and director of the Creativity and Emotions Lab at the Yale Center for Emotional Intelligence,
sentences.zh: 普林格尔博士是耶鲁大学情绪智能中心的资深研究科学家兼创意与情绪实验室主任，

sentences.en: where she studies the role of emotion in creativity and well-being.
sentences.zh: 她在那里研究情绪在创造力和幸福感中的作用。

sentences.en: Dr. Pringle is an APA fellow and has published more than 150 research studies in top academic journals.
sentences.zh: 普林格尔博士是美国心理学协会（APA）会士，已在顶级学术期刊上发表了150多项研究成果。

sentences.en: Her work has been covered by media outlets, including NPR, the Harvard Business Review,
sentences.zh: 她的工作受到了各大媒体的报道，包括NPR、《哈佛商业评论》、

sentences.en: Forbes, and many others.
sentences.zh: 《福布斯》以及许多其他媒体。

sentences.en: Her most recent book is called The Creativity Choice, The Science of Making Decisions to
sentences.zh: 她最近出版的一本书名为《创意的选择：将想法付诸行动的决策科学》（The Creativity Choice, The Science of Making Decisions to

sentences.en: Turn Ideas into Action.
sentences.zh: 将想法付诸行动。

sentences.en: Dr. Pringle, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 普林格尔博士，非常感谢你今天作客我们的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: So as I said, your book is called The Creativity Choice, and that framing is interesting because a lot of people think of creativity as something you either have or you don't.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，你的书名叫《创意的选择》，这个框架很有意思，因为很多人认为创造力要么生来就有，要么就没有。

sentences.en: So what do you mean by calling creativity a choice, and how does that change the way we think about our own creative potential?
sentences.zh: 那么，你将创造力称为一种“选择”是什么意思？这又将如何改变我们对自身创造潜能的看法？

sentences.en: You have mentioned several things that are really important to follow on.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到的好几个点都非常值得深入探讨。

sentences.en: We tend to think of creativity as something that we either have or you don't have.
sentences.zh: 我们往往认为创造力是那种要么天生拥有、要么天生没有的东西。

sentences.en: You see how people talk about it in our everyday lives.
sentences.zh: 你可以从日常生活中人们的言谈中看出来这一点。

sentences.en: When I introduce myself at a party and people learn that I study creativity, often I hear, oh, that is so interesting, but I did not get the creativity gene in the family.
sentences.zh: 当我在派对上自我介绍，大家得知我研究创造力时，经常听到有人说：“哦，这太有趣了，但我家好像没有遗传到创造力基因。”

sentences.en: that is then insert a relation or a friend who inevitably do something that is artistic
sentences.zh: 然后就会顺理成章地搬出一个亲戚或朋友，他们总会做出一些艺术品，

sentences.en: or in design or in these fields that we label as creative and even we use the word creative as a
sentences.zh: 或者搞设计，或者从事我们贴上“富有创意”标签的领域，甚至我们把“富有创意”当作一个

sentences.en: noun as if some people are that and other people are not and what psychologists really mean by
sentences.zh: 名词来用，好像有些人就是那种人而其他人不是一样。但心理学家真正所指的

sentences.en: creativity something much broader it is something that is in the same time both original and
sentences.zh: 创造力要广泛得多，它是一种同时兼具原创性又

sentences.en: effective in a way and what that original and effective means varies depending on the level
sentences.zh: 切实有效的东西，而这种原创且有效具体意味着什么，取决于我们讨论的是哪个层面的

sentences.en: of creativity we are discussing whether that is something in the learning process or something in
sentences.zh: 创造力，无论是学习过程中的某种事物，还是我们日常生活中、

sentences.en: our everyday life in our professional life or something that can make a big difference in the culture at large.
sentences.zh: 职业生涯中的事物，亦或是能够对整个文化产生重大影响的事物。

sentences.en: To help our listeners and me, I'm going to ask you how you define creativity because in my reading of your book, you focus on being able to do something novel and that the
sentences.zh: 为了帮助我们的听众和我自己，我要请教你如何定义创造力，因为在我读你的书时，你着重于能够做一些新颖的事情，并且

sentences.en: execution of the idea is critical to creativity.
sentences.zh: 想法的执行对于创造力至关重要。

sentences.en: Am I understanding you right?
sentences.zh: 我的理解对吗？

sentences.en: You are understanding it very much right.
sentences.zh: 你的理解非常正确。

sentences.en: It's an important point that creativity is not just having ideas.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很关键的观点，即创造力不仅仅是拥有点子。

sentences.en: There are lots of people who have ideas.
sentences.zh: 有许多人都很有想法。

sentences.en: We have all sat in brainstorming sessions and ideas are flying.
sentences.zh: 我们都参加过头脑风暴会议，各种点子满天飞。

sentences.en: So it's not that lack of creativity that we see in the world is because we don't have those.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们在世界上看到的缺乏创造力，并不是因为我们缺乏这些点子。

sentences.en: It is something else.
sentences.zh: 问题出在别的地方。

sentences.en: It is something that people sometimes call execution, but I think there is much more behind that term than meets the eye.
sentences.zh: 那是人们有时称之为“执行”的东西，但我认为这个词背后的内涵远比表面上看到的要丰富得多。

sentences.en: It is a process of making first the decision of whether you are going to engage with it
sentences.zh: 这是一个过程，首先要做出决定，看你是否要着手去做，

sentences.en: or not, whether it is worth engaging in something that might be carrying some risks, some psychological
sentences.zh: 是否值得去投入一件可能会带来某些风险的事情——某些心理风险、

sentences.en: risks uh risk to your reputation risks to how you see yourself can you rise to the challenge
sentences.zh: 对你声誉的风险、对你自我认知的风险。你能否迎接挑战？

sentences.en: that's an important decision it's a very first decision in engaging in creative work but then
sentences.zh: 这是一个重大的决定，是投入创造性工作时迈出的第一步；但随后的

sentences.en: each different branching is another choice that we can make towards something that is more conventional and easier, essentially easier because there's a blueprint in how to do it,
sentences.zh: 每一个不同分叉，都是我们可以做出的又一次选择：是走向更传统、更容易的道路（本质上因为有现成的蓝图可循），

sentences.en: or something that is more unconventional, has a greater potential for being original, but can be frustrating, can be challenging.
sentences.zh: 还是走向更非传统、更有可能具有原创性，但也可能令人沮丧、充满挑战的道路。

sentences.en: And we need some emotional skill to address it, to get us through that process.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一些情绪调节能力来应对它，从而度过这个过程。

sentences.en: Do you have any favorite examples of creativity in action, especially forms of creativity that people might overlook or not really recognize as creativity?
sentences.zh: 你有没有哪些特别喜欢的创意实践案例？特别是那些人们可能会忽略、或并不真正认出是创意的形式？

sentences.en: We can look at creativity in different contexts.
sentences.zh: 我们可以从不同的语境下来看待创造力。

sentences.en: So we can look at creativity in the learning process, and that is making a connection between something that you are studying
sentences.zh: 我们可以审视学习过程中的创造力，那是在你正在研究的事物

sentences.en: and something from a personal experience or from other domains of knowledge that you're already familiar with.
sentences.zh: 与你个人的经验或你已经熟悉的其它领域的知识之间建立联系。

sentences.en: Those new insights are a form of creativity.
sentences.zh: 这些新的见解就是一种创造力的形式。

sentences.en: Or we can look at creativity in our everyday lives, solving everyday challenges.
sentences.zh: 或者我们也可以看看日常生活中的创造力，去解决日常生活中遇到的挑战。

sentences.en: And we all carry very busy schedules.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人的日程都排得满满当当。

sentences.en: We have really difficult things we are trying to juggle at any given time.
sentences.zh: 在任何特定时间，我们都有许多极其棘手的事情需要兼顾。

sentences.en: To give you a personal example,
sentences.zh: 举个我自己的例子，

sentences.en: A few years ago, we were facing this challenge of how to arrange our summer travel because my husband and I are academics and have conferences and obligations.
sentences.zh: 几年前，我们面临着如何安排暑期旅行的挑战，因为我和丈夫都是学者，都有会议和各种事务要应付。

sentences.en: Our child was too young to be traveling on his own, but we wanted him to visit his grandparents in Europe.
sentences.zh: 我们的孩子太小，不能独自旅行，但我们希望他去欧洲看望爷爷奶奶。

sentences.en: And it seemed that these things cannot be integrated.
sentences.zh: 看起来这些事情似乎无法兼顾。

sentences.en: how are we going to make it all happen do we have to make a choice that we don't want to make
sentences.zh: 我们该怎么实现这一切？我们是否必须做出不愿做出的抉择，

sentences.en: choose something and not something else and then my husband did something that he does a lot and
sentences.zh: 选择做这个而放弃那个？然后我丈夫做了一件他经常做的事，

sentences.en: he says wait a second how can we approach this as a creative problem and once he said that
sentences.zh: 他说：“等等，我们怎么能把这当作一个创意问题来解决呢？”一旦他这么说了，

sentences.en: we started thinking in a different way we broke the problem in unobvious ways so instead of saying
sentences.zh: 我们就开始用不同的方式思考。我们以非显而易见的方式拆解了这个难题：与其说

sentences.en: both parents have to travel with a child we solve the problem as one parent takes the child to Europe
sentences.zh: 父母双方都必须陪孩子旅行，我们解决问题的方式改成：由一个家长带孩子去欧洲，

sentences.en: and the other parent takes him back and it became possible to solve this really complicated problem
sentences.zh: 另一个家长把他接回来。于是，以非常有创意的方式解决这个极其复杂的问题

sentences.en: in a creative way right with the mindset of creativity or to give you an unusual very unusual example from professional life.
sentences.zh: 便成了可能，这就是创意的思维方式。或者我再给你举一个职业生活中非常不寻常的例子。

sentences.en: We think of creativity in professional life as designers and R&D people.
sentences.zh: 我们通常认为职业生活中的创意属于设计师和研发人员。

sentences.en: What about a supervisor in a food services department of a hospital?
sentences.zh: 那医院餐饮部门的主管呢？

sentences.en: Would you imagine that they could be creative?
sentences.zh: 你能想象他们也能很有创意吗？

sentences.en: Not immediately.
sentences.zh: 不会马上想到。

sentences.en: Not immediately, right?
sentences.zh: 不会马上想到，对吧？

sentences.en: But this is what happened this person was noticing that his workers were getting burned out essentially
sentences.zh: 但事情是这样的：这个人注意到他的员工基本上都快精疲力竭了，

sentences.en: burned out they were getting frustrated it was they were getting tired and they were very unhappy
sentences.zh: 筋疲力尽，他们感到沮丧、疲惫，而且非常不开心，

sentences.en: and also they were making mistakes and these mistakes matter in this context because food is
sentences.zh: 此外他们还频频出错。在这个环境下，这些错误至关重要，因为食物

sentences.en: part of treatment you don't want to be making mistakes and getting wrong people to wrong food
sentences.zh: 是治疗的一部分，你绝不能出错，更不能把错误的食物送给错误的人。

sentences.en: to run people and so he said what can I learn from observing their points of frustration that's where emotions matter and unexpected emotions matter and he observed and realized
sentences.zh: 因此他说：“我能从观察他们的沮丧点中学到什么？”这就是情绪发挥作用的地方，也是意料之外的情绪发挥作用的地方。他通过观察意识到，

sentences.en: that he can redesign the workflow and he completely redesigned it to the point that people did not
sentences.zh: 他可以重新设计工作流程，并且他彻底对其进行了重新设计，以至于员工们

sentences.en: have to stretch anymore to get different iteMs. It was more convenient and they were not overexerting physically.
sentences.zh: 再也不需要费力够取不同的物品了。这变得更加便利，他们的身体也没有过度劳累。

sentences.en: Burnout was diminished greatly.
sentences.zh: 职业倦怠大大减轻了。

sentences.en: The mistakes were reduced and he was very unexpectedly creative.
sentences.zh: 错误减少了，而他的创造力出乎所有人意料。

sentences.en: Now, creativity seems like a difficult thing to study experimentally.
sentences.zh: 现在看来，创造力似乎是一件很难通过实验进行研究的事情。

sentences.en: How do you and other researchers measure and study creativity in a lab or in the real world?
sentences.zh: 你和其他研究人员是如何在实验室或现实世界中衡量和研究创造力的？

sentences.en: That is a great question and a very challenging one because creativity is something that in the real world can take hours, days, weeks, months.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题，也是一个极具挑战性的问题，因为创造力在现实世界中可能需要花费几小时、几天、几周甚至几个月的时间。

sentences.en: We are scientists and scientists from having an idea for a study to publishing it can take several years, actually.
sentences.zh: 我们是科学家，科学家从产生研究想法到发表论文，实际上可能需要好几年。

sentences.en: So how do we get that?
sentences.zh: 那么我们该如何做到这一点呢？

sentences.en: Well, in the lab, we can study certain parts of the creative process.
sentences.zh: 在实验室里，我们可以研究创意过程的某些部分。

sentences.en: So we can study how people come up with ideas in an experimental setting.
sentences.zh: 比如我们可以研究人们在实验环境中是如何想出点子的。

sentences.en: But we are also very fortunate to live at a time when we can have technology that makes it possible to study people as they work on something long term.
sentences.zh: 但我们也非常幸运，生活在一个拥有先进技术的时代，这使我们在人们长期从事某项工作时研究他们成为可能。

sentences.en: So we have technology of experience sampling.
sentences.zh: 所以我们拥有了体验采样技术。

sentences.en: We get notifications on people's phones that ask them, hey, what are you doing right now in this moment?
sentences.zh: 我们会向人们的手机发送通知，询问他们：“嘿，此时此刻你正在做什么？”

sentences.en: Are you working on different projects?
sentences.zh: “你是在进行不同的项目吗？”

sentences.en: Are you collecting information?
sentences.zh: “你是在收集信息吗？”

sentences.en: Are you in a meeting with collaborators?
sentences.zh: “你是在与合作者开会吗？”

sentences.en: What is your experience like right now?
sentences.zh: “你现在的体验是什么样的？”

sentences.en: And what are you thinking about?
sentences.zh: “你在想些什么？”

sentences.en: And then we can piece those pieces of information together and follow it through time.
sentences.zh: 然后我们可以把这些信息片段拼凑起来，并随着时间推移进行追踪。

sentences.en: How does creativity relate to problem solving?
sentences.zh: 创造力与解决问题之间有什么关系？

sentences.en: Are they essentially the same thing or is there something distinct about creative problem solving?
sentences.zh: 它们本质上是同一回事，还是说创造性解决问题有什么独特之处？

sentences.en: I think that often in our everyday conversation, we equate creativity and creative problem solving or complex problem solving.
sentences.zh: 我认为在日常对话中，我们经常把创造力与创造性问题解决或复杂问题解决等同起来。

sentences.en: And there are similarities for sure.
sentences.zh: 它们肯定有相似之处。

sentences.en: but the term creativity I think is broader than problem solving.
sentences.zh: 但我认为“创造力”这个词比“解决问题”更广泛。

sentences.en: Would you say that Monet was solving a problem when he was painting the water lilies?
sentences.zh: 你会说莫奈在画睡莲时是在解决问题吗？

sentences.en: We would probably not quite use that.
sentences.zh: 我们可能不会完全这样表述。

sentences.en: Would you say that you were solving a problem when you decide to invent a new game with your child, probably we would not use that.
sentences.zh: 你会说你决定和孩子发明一个新游戏时是在解决问题吗？我们大概也不会这样用。

sentences.en: Or in children's forms of creativity, are they solving a problem when they are engaging in pretend play, that foundational form of creativity in early childhood?
sentences.zh: 或者在儿童形式的创造力中，当他们进行假装游戏（幼儿期创造力的基础形式）时，他们是在解决问题吗？

sentences.en: So I think the concept of creativity is broader, but it includes problem solving.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为创造力的概念更广泛，但它包含了解决问题。

sentences.en: It includes creative problem solving and lots of the same processes are involved in it, both cognitive and emotional.
sentences.zh: 它包含了创造性问题解决，并且其中涉及许多相同的过程，既有认知的，也有情绪的。

sentences.en: I know you've been asked this question before, but I'm going to repeat it because I think it's a good one.
sentences.zh: 我知道以前有人问过你这个问题，但我还是要重复一遍，因为我觉得这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: What's the difference between producing a one-hit wonder and having consistent creativity?
sentences.zh: 打造一首“一曲成名”的歌曲与具备持续的创造力之间有什么区别？

sentences.en: Is the creator of a single hit, whatever that might be, less creative or just lucky?
sentences.zh: 单曲 hit 的创作者（无论那是什么）是缺乏创造力，还是只是运气好？

sentences.en: Oh, I love that question because it is one of those questions where there isn't a single answer and as a scientist studying creativity i like when there
sentences.zh: 哦，我很喜欢这个问题，因为它是那种没有单一答案的问题，而作为一个研究创造力的科学家，我很喜欢没有单一答案的

sentences.en: isn't a single answer um so uh i think a key difference between uh doing something consistently
sentences.zh: 问题。嗯……所以，我认为持续做一件事

sentences.en: and being a one-hit wonder is uh in the social side of creativity having the social infrastructure
sentences.zh: 与成为“一曲成名”的昙花一现者之间的关键区别在于，创造力的社会层面：拥有能够支持

sentences.en: that can support, okay, you had one idea, you have one product, you have contributed something.
sentences.zh: ——好吧，你有一个点子，你有一个产品，你做出了一些贡献——的社会基础设施。
